scope: Proposed component boundaries, verified by inert contracts; no production runtime or published package is created.

costs: Shared package exports must enforce a static-only CLI closure
Runtime authority and dependency growth can accidentally reach CLI startup
alternatives.disposition: considered; package count alone does not prove startup isolation

advantages: Separately versioned static validation and host authority
No FFI or subprocess backend for validation
costs: More artifact/provenance records and dependency inventories
alternatives.disposition: preferred boundary proposal; final language remains tied to qualified measurements and scorecards

advantages: Independent host implementation choices remain possible
A versioned protocol can isolate authority
costs: Duplicate semantic/version ownership or an additional protocol boundary
Two toolchain and supply-chain maintenance paths
No measured future host/FFI/IPC workload exists
alternatives.disposition: not selected for initial development; no unsupported bridge-performance claim

versionDomains.host: future design only; no runtime compatibility promise
versionDomains.adaptersAndExtensions: inert declarations only; executable ABI unsupported

startup: CLI statically imports spec/validation only; privileged host/catalog/broker/store constructors are unavailable. Import maps reject reverse edges. Native OS tests independently deny actual forbidden effects.
ownership: Alexander Agafonov under the existing bounded NF-101 single-maintainer acknowledgement; pre-release best effort, no invented SLA, backup, signing credentials or on-call commitment.
boundaryProofLimit: The graph and version-pair checks prove the proposed inert contract. They do not assert that future packages/runtime have been implemented or certified.
